scenario_summary: Customer is disputing an unrecognized $76 charge on her account and requesting a refund if unauthorized.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Mei Li and I'm 80. I noticed a $76 charge on my account from two days ago that I don't recognize. I haven't made any recent purchases that I can think of, though it's possible I forgot about something small. Can you look into it, and if it turns out I really didn't authorize it, can you refund it?

Hello, Ms. Li. I would be happy to help you investigate this charge. To get started, could you please provide your full account number and the zip code associated with your billing address for security verification?
Of course. My account number is 8829-4401-2093 and my zip code is 90210.

Thank you, Ms. Li. I have verified your identity. I see the transaction you are referring to: it is a $76.00 charge from 'Global Tech Services' dated two days ago. Does that name sound familiar, or would you like me to pull up the merchant contact details for you?
No, that name doesn't mean anything to me at all. I haven't bought any technology services recently.

I understand. Under our 'Unauthorized Transaction Protection' policy, if a charge is confirmed as unauthorized, we can initiate a formal dispute. I have reviewed the transaction metadata, and since the charge originated from a source that does not match your typical spending patterns, I am authorized to process a provisional credit immediately while we investigate.
Oh, that would be a relief. Will I get my money back today?

Yes, I have just processed the refund of $76.00 to your account. You should see the credit reflected in your balance within the next hour. I have also officially opened a dispute case for this transaction, and our fraud department will send you a letter via mail within 3-5 business days with the final resolution details.

resolution_summary: Agent verified the account, confirmed the charge was inconsistent with spending patterns, and issued a full refund under the Unauthorized Transaction Protection policy.
